headline: South Asia: Pakistani national killed, 11 wounded as Riyadh airport hit by Houthi strike
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistani national killed, 11 wounded as Riyadh airport hit by Houthi strike.
- Southern Europe: NATO’s Top Commander Unveils Plan for Victory Against Russia.
- Asia: US turns to low-cost Blackbeard hypersonic missiles to overwhelm Chinese defences.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Vector, Nammo expand push to mass-produce armed drones.
- Military Times, 5 hours ago: Vector, Nammo expand push to mass-produce armed drones.
Executives from both companies say they’re scaling up production of systems that reflect “the realities of how warfighters will employ them.”
The Caribbean - bottom line: Harris wants early guilty pleas to count in more cases.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Harris wants early guilty pleas to count in more cases.
President of the Advocates’ Association of Jamaica (AAJ), Tamika Harris, is calling for greater recognition of early guilty pleas in Jamaica’s criminal justice system, arguing that they can spare victims further trauma and help reduce court backlogs. “Encouraging early guilty pleas is not about rewarding criminal conduct. It is about promoting accountability, protecting victims and ensuring the timely administration of justice.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Appeal court slashes trespass award in Manchester land row.
THE COURT of Appeal has slashed a $400,000 damages award to $150,000 while upholding a finding of trespass against the Simmonds family in a long-standing Manchester land dispute between neighbouring families. The Morgan family – comprising Marylyn Morgan, her sister Melva Morgan, and her son Jason Salmon – took the Simmonds family to court in 2017, alleging trespass after members of the family began constructing a house on land in Swaby’s Hope, Spur Tree, Manchester, which the Morgans claimed to have possessed and used for over 40 years.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE

- Balkan Insight, just now: NATO’s Top Commander Unveils Plan for Victory Against Russia.
The strategy draws on lessons from Ukraine, putting cheap drones, AI and rapid military strikes at the heart of NATO's response to any Russian attack.
- Politico Europe, just now: EU approves biggest Russia sanctions package since invasion began.
“This is the single largest expansion of our sanctions list since Russia started its war," Kaja Kallas said.
- Politico Europe, 3 hours ago: Trump’s NATO envoy calls for moving military forces east as US reviews troops in Europe.
Matthew Whitaker called for an overhaul of NATO’s bases and military infrastructure to move forces eastward as America reviews its troop presence in Europe.
- Politico Europe, just now: French supermarkets face food crisis after cyberattack hits refrigerators.
France's cyber agency coordinating with European counterparts in response to hackers.
Western Russia - bottom line: Family with child killed in Russian rocket artillery strike on Cherkaske in Donetsk Oblast.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Family with child killed in Russian rocket artillery strike on Cherkaske in Donetsk Oblast.
Three people, including a child, have been killed and four others injured as a result of Russian strikes on the settlement of Cherkaske in Donetsk Oblast on the morning of 12 October.
- The Moscow Times, 3 hours ago: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks.
The strikes on Yandex data centers have caused server outages that triggered service disruptions for users.
- The Moscow Times, just now: Ukraine’s Strikes on Yandex Data Centers, Explained.
Drone strikes on Yandex data centers are disrupting services from taxis to digital payments across Russia.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Kremlin ready for one-day ceasefire for Ukraine's elections but dismisses 60-day proposal.
Dmitry Peskov, press secretary for the Russian leader, has stated that Russia is unwilling to observe a 60-day ceasefire for elections in Ukraine, but Vladimir Putin is supposedly ready to halt strikes only on election day.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Houthi rebels claim new strikes on Saudi airports and energy facilities.
- Africanews, 6 hours ago: Houthi rebels claim new strikes on Saudi airports and energy facilities.
Major airports in Saudi Arabia were hit by fresh attacks on Sunday, killing one person and injuring 11 others at King Khalid International Airport in the capital Riyadh.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 9 hours ago: Sudan: Air Strikes Kill Dozens of Gold Miners on Sudan-Egypt Border.
[DW] A Sudan-based rights group said 72 people were killed in a remote, disputed area known for illegal gold mining.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 10 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan Condemns Suicide Drone Attacks On El-Obeid.
[SNA] Khartoum (SUNA) - The Government of the Republic of Sudan strongly condemned the attacks carried out against the city of El-Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan State, on Friday using suicide drones, attributed to the rebel Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia. According to preliminary information, the attacks resulted in civilian injuries and damage to homes and property.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 3 hours ago: Somalia: Somalia's Former Prime Minister Warns of Risks From Military Moves Near Former Leaders' Homes.
[Shabelle] Mogadishu, Somalia -- Former Somali prime minister Hassan Ali Khaire has warned that military movements targeting the homes of former national leaders in Mogadishu could fuel instability and deepen the country's political crisis.

- Jerusalem Post, just now: One killed, children among 19 wounded after ordnance explodes during northern Israel school trip.

Trump's energy truce sparks criticism over aiding Russia's war finances amid diesel shortages and rising consumer costs.

[SAnews.gov.za] Government has warned that individuals using social media to incite violence, intimidate foreign nationals or mobilise unlawful activities will face the consequences of their actions as tensions surrounding migration and asylum applications continue.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 9 hours ago: Nigeria: Xenophobia - 111 More Distressed Nigerians Return From South Africa.
[Daily Trust] Another batch of 111 distressed Nigerians have returned from South Africa following the xenophobic attacks in the country.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 10 hours ago: Mozambique: Chapo Calls for Voluntary Surrender of Illegal Firearms Before December Deadline.
[AIM] Maputo -- Mozambican President Daniel Francisco Chapo has warned that the authorities will forcibly collect illegally held firearms after December, when the deadline for their voluntary surrender, under a police amnesty programme, expires.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistani national killed, 11 wounded as Riyadh airport hit by Houthi strike.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, Al Jazeera - Middle East, Taipei Times, one hour ago: Pakistani national killed, 11 wounded as Riyadh airport hit by Houthi strike.
A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, killing one person — a Pakistani resident — and wounding 11 others, a day after another deadly attack claimed by the Yemeni group forced authorities to suspend operations there. Saturday’s attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh has long militarily supported the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 19 hours ago: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in KP as president approves cabinet decision.
Key developments: Emergency imposed under Article 232, governor’s rule under Article 234 Cabinet recommended move due to KP govt’s ‘deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism’ Technocratic council formed; Fakhr Alam appointed as KP chief secretary PTI’s Gohar condemns decision as undemocratic, says peace cannot be established by weakening provincial autonomy Governor Kundi calls for unity for ‘new chapter’ in KP’s development ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the president’s approval of the recomme
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: DPM Dar defends emergency and governor's rule in KP, says measures not politically motivated.
A day after the government imposed governor’s rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar defended the move, saying it was not politically motivated but instead taken to curb terrorism. DPM Dar made the comments while addressing a seminar in Islamabad, a day after the federal government imposed emergency under Article 232 and the governor’s rule under Article 234 in KP. The Cabinet recommended the move, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”.
- The Hindu - International, NK News, Yonhap News Agency, 2 hours ago: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles, adding to streak of weapons tests.
While maintaining a hard line toward Seoul, North Korea has been ramping up weapons testing as it seeks to expand its arsenal of nuclear-capable systems
Asia - bottom line: US turns to low-cost Blackbeard hypersonic missiles to overwhelm Chinese defences.
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: US turns to low-cost Blackbeard hypersonic missiles to overwhelm Chinese defences.
The US Navy aims to field a relatively low-cost hypersonic missile on its carrier-based fighters, a weapon that could pose a new challenge to the air defences protecting Chinese warships and coastal military installations, experts said. California-based defence company Castelion’s Blackbeard is designed to fly at more than five times the speed of sound and strike ships and land targets. Unlike more expensive hypersonic weapons, it is being developed with an emphasis on affordability and mass...
- South China Morning Post - China, just now: France supermarkets say cyberattack forced defrosting of refrigerators in over 200 stores.
Major French supermarket chains Intermarché and Coopérative U were hit by a cyberattack that caused their refrigerators to defrost, the two retailers told AFP Monday. Some 150-200 Intermarché shops were targeted, along with almost 100 Coopérative U outlets, in the attack, they said. Paris prosecutors confirmed the attack, which reportedly also hit other major chains, and also indicated it had prompted outbreaks of fire. BFM TV said France’s largest supermarket chain E. Leclerc was also affected,...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: China, EU take a breath after surprise deal brings temporary halt to trade tussle.
Weeks of high-wire negotiations between China and the EU culminated in a surprise trade deal that will, among other measures, impose strict quotas on Chinese hybrid car exports to the bloc and slash Chinese tariffs on a variety of European goods. The deal, unveiled on Friday, takes some of the heat out of searing bilateral trade tensions and temporarily averts the prospect of a bruising trade war – a cooldown augmented by Beijing’s subsequent reduction of value-added tax (VAT) export rebates on...
- South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: UK comedian Russell Brand in London court for rape trial start.
Jury selection took place on Monday for the ⁠trial of British actor ⁠and comedian Russell Brand over alleged ⁠historical crimes including rape and other sexual offences. Brand, 51, once one of Britain’s most high-profile broadcasters and former husband of US singer Katy Perry, faces three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and ‌one count of indecent assault relating to six women from 1999 to 2009. Brand has denied all the accusations. He arrived at London’s Southwark Crown Court...
India - bottom line: Zelenskyy says Russia strikes Ukraine energy sites despite Trump’s ceasefire claim.
- Times of India - Top Stories, Ukrainska Pravda, The Hindu - International, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Zelenskyy says Russia strikes Ukraine energy sites despite Trump’s ceasefire claim.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Anthropic, OpenAI prepare for AI disaster that could shut down internet, power, water.
Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI companies are privately war-gaming the political fallout of a catastrophic AI event, Axios reports. Executives fear a major cyberattack could knock out banking, internet, power and water, with insiders expecting an incident within six to 12 months. The firms are red-teaming worst-case scenarios and briefing Congress to shape future AI rules, with Democrats eyeing a crackdown after the November midterms.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: The Himalayas are getting a new war machine as Indian Army expands its drone arsenal.
The Indian Army has ordered 225 First-Person View drones aimed at enhancing operational capabilities in Ladakh. These drones will be provided by Gurgaon-based Aerodrone Robotics Pvt Ltd following successful trials at high altitudes. Increasing drone deployment is part of the Army's modernization efforts in response to regional tensions and warfare evolution. The drones are expected to improve surveillance and logistics in challenging terrains.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: ‘Goddess of bombs’: Tanot Mata temple in Jaisalmer sees massive Navratri turnout.
Tanot Mata Temple near the India-Pakistan border is significant to soldiers and civilians, especially during Navratri. Thousands of devotees have started visiting the shrine to seek blessings from Tanot Mata. The temple is known for its association with unexploded bombs during past wars. Security personnel have strengthened arrangements to facilitate the large number of pilgrims visiting the temple.
